criteria.observation: At T1, the assistant explicitly identified “better” as underspecified, quantified the trade-off between time and correctness, asked which of maintaining roughly 90% correctness or maximizing time savings was non-negotiable, and withheld a mechanism recommendation pending that clarification.

At T2, the assistant preserved the clarified priority that correctness must not be sacrificed, rejected autonomous replacement at the reported 65% rate, and proposed a bounded shadow-mode trial with staff review and a 90% correctness adoption threshold. It did not repeat the resolved outcome question.
